text:
Both responses are accurate on the key figures and dates: 84 staff, $3.9M, eight weeks, the one-quarter direction with eight weeks' notice, the two-week cash-out with four weeks remaining, the 24 December to 2 January shutdown, the warehouse exemption, and the 31 October list deadline. Neither has a substantive error.

Response B covers the shutdown more completely by including the unpaid leave and make-up time options, which matter to staff without enough leave. It also gives the burnout rationale and labels cash-out as new. Its main gap is describing the coverage as "permanent staff" without mentioning part-time staff, a minor omission. Response A's advantage is the "40 days for full-time" detail and a clearer statement of who is covered. It omits the unpaid and make-up options, which a manager would likely need to answer staff questions.

Both are close to the 120-word limit, so concision is roughly even. On balance, B keeps slightly more of what the reader needs.

Verdict: B
